item.title: South Korea: LG Uplus commits another 789 billion won to its 200 MW Paju AI data centre
item.description: LG Uplus disclosed on 19 November 2026 (regulatory filing, board approval the same day) a new facility investment of up to 789 billion won for the next phase of its Paju AI data centre in Gyeonggi Province, a fourth building, with spending scheduled from 23 November 2026 to 31 January 2029. The amount is an approval ceiling set at about 130% of the estimate and equals 8.7% of consolidated equity. Earlier commitments were 615.6 billion won (first building, April 2025) and 1.3 trillion won (second and third buildings, July 2026), taking disclosed Paju investment above 2.7 trillion won toward 200 MW across four buildings by 2028 (Chosun Biz; CBC Globe). Country conversion: Korean telco capacity keeps moving from plan to funded build, citing customer demand. [Signal 36, Corroborated, via LG Uplus regulatory disclosure, 19 Nov 2026; Chosun Biz; CBC Globe] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Israel: Mega Or signs Nebius for another 134 MW of IT capacity, one site still waiting on a grid connection
item.description: Mega Or's data centre arm Mega DC signed a third agreement with a Nebius subsidiary for 134 MW of IT capacity across MDCIL-4 in Beit Shemesh (under construction, grid connection approved, up to 135 MW IT) and MDCIL-7 in Masmiya, Yoav Regional Council (Calcalist, 19 Nov 2026). Masmiya has no grid approval yet and its application is frozen by the Electricity Authority; approval is a condition for finalising that part of the deal. Completion targeted by end of Q2 2028; seven-year term from delivery with a five-year extension option; estimated construction cost about $1.6 billion (about $12 million per MW IT) and NIS 550 million average annual NOI when full. Earlier deals covered 8 MW (Modi'in) and 80 MW (Beit Shemesh and Masmiya). Country conversion: Israel's neocloud pipeline is now gated by the Electricity Authority's connection queue. [Signal 32, Single-source, via Calcalist (Ctech), 19 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Jordan: digital economy minister previews a 400 MW Al-Risha data centre and a 200 MW AI campus
item.description: Jordan's Minister of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship Sami Smeirat told Arab News on 19 November 2026, at the Jordan-EU Investment Conference at the Dead Sea, that a package of announcements would include a 400 MW data centre in the Al-Risha area and a 200 MW AI campus, plus other data centres and university AI research upgrades. He expects the projects to add about 3.6 billion Jordanian dinars ($5 billion) to GDP. No developers, investors, timelines or power sources were given in the interview. Caveat: ministerial preview ahead of the formal announcements. Country conversion: Jordan enters the Gulf-adjacent pipeline on paper; conversion depends on named sponsors and power. [Signal 26, Single-source, via Arab News, 19 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: Anthropic prices the largest IPO on record at $83, raising $81.3 billion plus a $26 billion private placement
item.description: Anthropic priced its IPO on 18 November 2026 at $83 per Class A share, above the $70 to $78 marketed range: 980 million shares (956.4 million primary, 23.6 million from selling stockholders) for $81.34 billion, plus a concurrent $26.0 billion private placement of Class N stock at the same price (SEC pricing term sheet). Bloomberg puts the combined raise at $107.3 billion; CNBC and AP put the fully diluted value near $1.5 trillion. Shares trade on Nasdaq as ANT from 19 November; underwriters hold a 30-day option on 147 million more primary shares. Country conversion: the largest buyer of US compute outside the hyperscalers now has public-market access to fund leases and chips, at the same moment Nvidia is signalling more discipline on neocloud guarantees. [Signal 52, Confirmed, via Anthropic, 18 Nov 2026; SEC free writing prospectus; CNBC; AP; Bloomberg] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: transmission owners ask FERC to bind data centres to 10 to 20 year grid-upgrade contracts
item.description: Responding to FERC's June show-cause order on large-load interconnection, five of six grid operators had filed by 16 November (Southwest Power Pool is due 20 November), and the transmission-owning utilities filed their own cost proposals (Latitude Media, 18 Nov). In PJM, a data centre would sign a cost recovery agreement with the transmission owner paying at least 80% of requested transmission service for a minimum of 10 years, with collateral starting at 25% and rising to 100% by in-service, and an exit fee. California and New York propose 15-year terms; MISO proposes a three-way contract of up to 20 years. Comments on several filings are due 7 December; FERC rejected most of PJM's previous large-load plan in October. Country conversion: faster studies come with long take-or-pay obligations, pushing interconnection risk onto developers and their tenants. [Signal 42, Single-source, via Latitude Media, 18 Nov 2026, citing FERC filings] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: Nvidia discloses up to $118 billion of infrastructure guarantees while tightening terms for neoclouds
item.description: Nvidia's third-quarter filing shows maximum gross exposure of up to $118 billion in financial guarantees tied to AI infrastructure: up to $105 billion for SB Energy's PORTS-Pike campus in Ohio (about 4.25 GW, nine buildings, 20-year leases to OpenAI, first guarantee from fiscal 2029), $9.5 billion of power and systems credit support and $3.5 billion of land, power and shell guarantees for neocloud providers; no guarantee payments had been made as of 25 October (TechTarget). New footnote language says commitments to neoclouds take effect only once they secure financing and may be reduced or cancelled on data centre delays; Morgan Stanley says disclosed neocloud commitments fell to $32 billion from $36 billion and cut its deployment forecast to 4 GW from 5 GW (CNBC). CoreWeave and Iren fell about 3% on 18 November. Country conversion: US neocloud builds now need their own financing before Nvidia's backstop applies. [Signal 44, Corroborated, via CNBC, 18 Nov 2026; TechTarget, 18 Nov 2026; Nvidia Q3 FY27 filing] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: new data centre construction starts fell to 8.4 GW in Q3 from 11.2 GW, but October rebounded to 4.6 GW
item.description: Cleanview data reported by DCD on 18 November 2026 show US data centre construction starts of 8.4 GW in Q3 2026, down from a record 11.2 GW in Q2 and the first quarterly dip since Q1 2025. Starts in 2026 total 38 GW, double 2025, and October alone reached 4.6 GW, the highest since June. Cleanview counts 58 GW under construction against 65 GW operating, with Texas leading at 9.8 GW started in the last 12 months, then Virginia at 4.5 GW and Louisiana at 2.8 GW; Amazon (4.6 GW), Google (4.1 GW) and Meta (3.9 GW) were the top developers. Caveat: one tracker's methodology. Country conversion: the US pipeline under construction nearly equals its whole operating fleet. [Signal 34, Single-source, via DCD, 18 Nov 2026, citing Cleanview] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: Salt Lake City bans new data centres for 180 days
item.description: The Salt Lake City Council voted 6-0 (one member absent) on 17 November 2026 for a citywide 180-day ban on new data centres while it drafts rules on energy and water use, noise, heat and lighting; the ordinance cites the Great Salt Lake, air quality and high utility demand (Axios Salt Lake City, 18 Nov). Council members suspended the 24-hour agenda rule to pass the last-minute measure. It follows permit applications filed in September by Florida-based Qlevr LLC for a data centre in the Northpoint neighbourhood (Salt Lake Tribune, via Axios). Country conversion: a second US jurisdiction in one week stops new entitlements, after Loudoun County's 12-month pause. [Signal 30, Single-source, via Axios Salt Lake City, 18 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: Loudoun County, the world's largest data centre market, pauses new data centre and substation approvals for up to 12 months
item.description: Loudoun County's Board of Supervisors voted 7-1-1 on 17 November 2026 to stop acting on legislative applications (rezonings and special exceptions) for data centres and substations for up to 12 months, backdated to 15 September 2026, while it finishes Phase 2 of its data centre zoning standards (Loudoun Now; county agenda). Bisnow reports 33 active legislative applications are affected. Exempt: substations deemed necessary for grid reliability, applications in the Route 28 tax district, already-approved projects and administrative reviews such as site plans. After the pause, at most five backlog applications will be heard per meeting. The county attorney said a moratorium on a use is not legal in Virginia, so the board is using the 12-month review clock, and warned of a real litigation risk; DCD cites a county fact sheet putting data centre revenue at $1.3 billion, 40% of the 2027 budget. Country conversion: new entitlements in Data Center Alley stall until about September 2027, so capacity that is not already zoned shifts to other counties and states. [Signal 58, Confirmed, via Loudoun County Board of Supervisors agenda, 17 Nov 2026; Loudoun Now; Bisnow; WUSA9; DCD] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: Nvidia reports $115.8 billion quarter, guides $130 billion with no China data centre revenue and lifts next-year growth to 75%
item.description: Nvidia reported fiscal Q3 2027 (quarter ended 25 October 2026) revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year on year, with Data Center revenue of $107.6 billion, up 110%, and GAAP gross margin of 74.8% (company release, 17 November 2026). It guided Q4, which has an extra week, to $130.0 billion plus or minus 3% and said it assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China; gross margin is guided to 71% to 72%. Interim CEO Colette Kress raised the fiscal 2028 growth outlook to 75% from 70%, citing supply of chips, advanced packaging and memory, and the company said it would not take questions on Jensen Huang's resignation (Reuters, CNBC). Nvidia said Vera Rubin NVL72 has shipped, with racks running at CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Oracle and Nebius. Country conversion: US chip supply is not the constraint on capacity; power and permits are. [Signal 55, Confirmed, via Nvidia press release, 17 Nov 2026; Reuters; CNBC; Fortune] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Singapore: US Justice and Commerce confirm a criminal export-control investigation into Megaspeed, Southeast Asia's largest Nvidia buyer
item.description: In a joint statement dated 17 November 2026, the US Department of Justice and Department of Commerce said Commerce opened an investigation into Singapore-based Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations, requested records from Nvidia in May 2025, and that Nvidia put Megaspeed on its no-sell list in June 2025. BIS agents and Singapore law enforcement then carried out an on-site end-use check and interviewed then-CEO Alice Huang, after which DOJ took the lead on a criminal investigation. BBC describes Megaspeed as the biggest buyer of Nvidia chips in Southeast Asia; Politico notes it has not been added to the Entity List. Caveat: no charges announced. Country conversion: with the new BIS licence rule, GPU-heavy capacity in Singapore faces both a licence queue and heavier customer due diligence. [Signal 44, Confirmed, via DOJ and Commerce joint statement, 17 Nov 2026; BBC; Politico; CNBC] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: Texas resumes data centre environmental permits and clears SpaceX's Starbase gas plant, but Cameron County rejects its tax break
item.description: The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality resumed normal permit review on 16 November 2026 after notice from Governor Greg Abbott's office on 13 November, ending a pause he ordered in August, once ERCOT had gathered responses from 93% of 465 projects for a December report (DCD, citing the Texas Tribune). TCEQ then issued a major air permit for SpaceX's planned $24 billion gas-fired data centre at Starbase. On 17 November, Cameron County commissioners voted against holding another meeting on SpaceX's tax break request, so the abatement will not advance (DCD, citing local reporting). Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa, who campaigned on a moratorium, takes office in January 2027. Country conversion: Texas permits flow again for now, but local tax incentives and the incoming governor are the new gates. [Signal 40, Corroborated, via DCD, 18 Nov 2026, citing Texas Tribune; DCD on Cameron County, 18 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: India: Amazon commits $7 billion more to renewable power by 2030 and signs 934 MW of new PPAs
item.description: Amazon said on 17 November 2026 it will invest $7 billion in renewable energy projects in India by 2030, on top of $4 billion already contracted. It signed power purchase agreements with four projects totalling 934 MW: 234 MW of wind in Karnataka, a 200 MW solar and wind project in Karnataka, 300 MW of solar in Madhya Pradesh and 200 MW of solar in Rajasthan. Its India portfolio is now 14 utility-scale projects and 43 on-site solar installations. Developers and PPA lengths were not disclosed. Country conversion: a hyperscaler is pre-buying the clean power its Indian cloud regions need, the input that most often lags in Indian data centre buildouts. [Signal 32, Confirmed, via Amazon, 17 Nov 2026; DCD; Mint; Economic Times] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Australia: Macquarie Data Centres files for a 200 MW, AU$2 billion campus in Sydney's Macquarie Park
item.description: DCD reported on 17 November 2026 that Macquarie Data Centres has applied to the New South Wales government (SEARS) for the Macquarie Engineering and Technology Campus at 2 Alma Road, Macquarie Park: 200 MW across 42,015 square metres, up to six storeys, with about AU$2 billion (US$1.35 billion) of investment, replacing existing office buildings. No timeline was given. Macquarie today runs IC2 and IC3 East with IC3 Super West in development, 65 MW combined in Macquarie Park. Caveat: early planning filing. Country conversion: Sydney's operators keep densifying existing metro clusters while Firmus chases private money for its larger builds. [Signal 28, Single-source, via DCD, 17 Nov 2026, citing NSW SEARS application] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: Giga Energy signs a $1 billion, 10-year lease for its 60 MW Project Clay in Hunt County, Texas
item.description: Giga Energy announced on 17 November 2026 a $1 billion lease with an undisclosed US-based AI cloud provider for Project Clay, a 60 MW modular data centre in Hunt County, Texas, which it broke ground on in July and will develop, own and operate. It targets ready-for-service in spring 2027, uses closed-loop cooling with no water for compute, and taps underused dedicated power infrastructure rather than local distribution capacity. DCD gives the lease term as ten years. Hunt County is also where AMD is leasing 110 MW from Core Scientific. Country conversion: a second AI lease in the same Texas county in a week, built to the conditions the incoming governor has set out. [Signal 28, Confirmed, via Giga Energy, 17 Nov 2026; DCD] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Egypt: Vodafone Egypt, Elsewedy and Cassava form Africa Data Centres Egypt, 20 MW first and up to 200 MW
item.description: Vodacom's interim results for the six months to 30 September 2026 disclose a joint venture of Vodafone Egypt, Elsewedy Electric and Cassava Technologies, Africa Data Centres Egypt, to build what it calls Egypt's largest data centre and the country's first sovereign AI data centre. It targets 20 MW of initial capacity within three years, with potential to expand to 200 MW; phase one is expected to draw about $200 million of foreign direct investment, rising to $1 billion at full capacity (DCD, 17 Nov). Caveat: no site, power source or anchor tenant disclosed. Country conversion: Egypt gets a named telco-industrial-backed AI build with a stated MW path, starting small. [Signal 34, Confirmed, via Vodacom interim results (Nov 2026); Vodacom newsroom; DCD, 17 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Greece: the state's new sovereign fund takes 23% of Data4 Greece, its first digital-infrastructure deal
item.description: DCD reported on 17 November 2026 that the Hellenic Innovation & Infrastructure Fund (HIIF), the investment arm of the Hellenic Growth Fund, has taken a 23% minority stake in Data4 Greece. Brookfield-owned Data4 is building the ATH1 campus at Paiania near Athens: 90 MW across two data centres at full build-out and more than €300 million of investment; the first 15 MW phase went live in July 2026 and the campus is fully leased to an unnamed major international tech company. HIIF was seeded with €300 million. Caveat: price not disclosed. Country conversion: Greece's state capital is now co-investing in leased data-centre capacity rather than only offering incentives. [Signal 30, Single-source, via DCD, 17 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Sweden: Nokia, Nscale, Telia, Verda and Skeleton form AIGF Northern to bid for an EU AI gigafactory
item.description: DCD reported on 17 November 2026 that Nokia, Nscale, Skeleton, Telia and Verda formed AI Gigafactory Northern (AIGF Northern), a consortium that intends to bid in the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking's AI gigafactory call. Planned sites are Oulu (Finland), Iru (Estonia) and Valmiera (Latvia), with a Swedish site still to be chosen. Roles: Nokia networks, Nscale and Verda AI cloud, Telia connectivity and operations, Skeleton high-power systems. Caveat: a bid consortium only, with no MW, capex or power contracts disclosed; Lot 2 bids are due 3 December. Country conversion: the Nordic-Baltic corridor enters the EU gigafactory race as one multi-country bid rather than competing national ones. [Signal 32, Single-source, via DCD, 17 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: PJM files to study data centre load and new generation together in a single one-year process
item.description: PJM filed its Fast Energization proposal with FERC at the end of 16 November 2026 (docket ER27-531). It would study generation interconnection and transmission service for large loads such as data centres together, cutting the projected timeline from two years to one, move readiness and financial requirements earlier to weed out speculative projects, create new transmission services including for loads willing to limit grid use, and give states the cost of upgrades driven by large loads so they can bill them. PJM asked for a 60-day comment period and a FERC order within 120 days; it also filed separate ride-through requirements so data centres stay connected during grid disturbances. Country conversion: the largest US grid region is trying to halve the wait from signed load to energised capacity, at the price of stricter upfront deposits. [Signal 46, Confirmed, via PJM Inside Lines, 16 Nov 2026; FERC eLibrary ER27-531; Utility Dive] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Israel: Enlight and Shemen plan a data centre of up to 150 MW in Haifa
item.description: Nasdaq-listed Enlight Renewable Energy and Shemen Yielding Real Estate announced on 16 November 2026 an agreement to develop, finance, build and operate a data centre of up to 150 MW on Shemen's land at Hof Shemen in Haifa, through a 50:50 project company led by Enlight, with a lease term of about 25 years. A 150 MW grid connection application has been filed; the final site size depends on grid capacity and approvals. Enlight has an option to buy 50% of the land at no less than NIS 6.3 million per dunam (DCD). Caveat: no tenant, timeline or final approvals yet. Country conversion: an Israeli power developer is moving into data centres with a grid application in hand. [Signal 30, Confirmed, via Enlight (GlobeNewswire), 16 Nov 2026; DCD; Calcalist] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: BIS rule makes advanced AI chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil license-only and controls remote access for China-headquartered customers
item.description: The Bureau of Industry and Security released an interim final rule on 16 November 2026, which it says was written at the direction of Treasury and the National Security Council, to stop export controls being sidestepped through remote access to data centres in third countries. A license is now required to export, reexport or transfer advanced semiconductors to or within Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, reviewed case by case; the requirement does not apply where the consignee or its ultimate parent is headquartered in the United States and the exporter meets new monthly reporting rules (section 743.10). Separately, a license is needed for chips going to any data centre worldwide that will give more than 12 million aggregate TPP of compute, at one site or across linked sites, to companies headquartered in China, other D:5 destinations or Macau, with know-your-customer diligence expected from the data centre (Nixon Peabody reading of the rule). Nixon Peabody says Federal Register publication is expected on 19 November and existing arrangements get 90 days to obtain a license. China's foreign ministry criticised the rule on 17 November (NBC). Country conversion: in the five named countries, AI capacity built for non-US-headquartered tenants now sits behind a US license queue, while US hyperscalers keep a reporting-only path. [Signal 62, Confirmed, via BIS press release, 16 Nov 2026; Federal Register public inspection (RIN 0694-AK50); Nixon Peabody; NBC News] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: OpenAI signs a six-year deal for 457 MW of AMD MI455X Helios capacity from TensorWave
item.description: TensorWave announced on 16 November 2026 (Business Wire) a six-year agreement to provide OpenAI with 457 MW of dedicated, single-tenant AI capacity across multiple US data centres, built on AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs in Helios rack-scale systems. First capacity is expected in the first half of 2027 and full deployment by early 2028. DCD notes TensorWave raised a $350 million Series B in June 2026 and claims 2 GW of long-term US capacity; its earlier lease at Fermi's Project Matador was terminated this month. Caveat: no contract value or sites disclosed. Country conversion: a second large AMD-based anchor in the US in a week, after AMD's own 110 MW lease with Core Scientific in Texas. [Signal 48, Confirmed, via TensorWave (Business Wire), 16 Nov 2026; DCD] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: Blackstone's listed REIT buys 75% of two AWS campuses (13 buildings, 647 MW) for about $5 billion at a 7% cap rate
item.description: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust (NYSE: BXDC) said on 16 November 2026 it signed a definitive agreement to acquire a 75% interest in two joint ventures with AWS that own 13 newly built powered shells across two AWS campuses, valued at about $5 billion at an initial 7.0% capitalization rate. AWS keeps 25% and leases back 100% triple net for an initial 12 years, extendable to 32. REBusinessOnline reports the 647 MW portfolio is nine buildings in northern Indiana and four in Mississippi, with debt covering half the price at closing. Closing is expected in Q4 2026. Country conversion: a hyperscaler is recycling capital out of finished US campuses into public-market REIT money, which frees AWS balance sheet for new builds. [Signal 46, Confirmed, via BXDC press release and 8-K, 16 Nov 2026; DCD; REBusinessOnline] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Australia: Firmus seeks $3 billion in private equity and customer prepayments after its pulled IPO
item.description: DCD, citing the Australian Financial Review and three unnamed sources, reported on 16 November 2026 that Australian neocloud Firmus is trying to raise $3 billion in equity and secure prepayments from large customers including Nvidia, OpenAI and Meta, which could fund up to 12.5% of contracts under development. Firmus had about 916 MW of contracted capacity and 46 MW operating as of September 2026; its IPO was pulled earlier, which the company blamed on market volatility. Its last private round raised $2 billion at a $10.5 billion post-money valuation. Caveat: single press report; Firmus has not confirmed terms. Country conversion: Australia's largest contracted AI build (Tasmania and mainland) now depends on customer cash, not public markets, to move from contract to energised capacity. [Signal 40, Single-source, via DCD, 16 Nov 2026, citing AFR] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: South Korea: SK Telecom locks Hyosung as supplier for 345 kV substation gear behind its gigawatt-scale AI data centres
item.description: Hyosung Heavy Industries and SK Telecom signed a strategic partnership MoU on 16 November 2026 at SKT Tower in Seoul (Hyosung newsroom). Hyosung will supply core equipment for the 345 kV substations serving SKT's AI data centres, and the two will coordinate production and delivery schedules in advance for long-lead items such as transformers. They will also test 800 V DC distribution and solid-state transformers and share substation O&M know-how. Seoul Economic Daily notes SKT targets 5 GW of AI data centre capacity by 2029 and 15 GW by 2035, per SKT's July plan. Caveat: an MoU with no volumes or value. Country conversion: Korea's largest AI build plan is reserving grid equipment ahead of sites, the step that most often delays capacity. [Signal 30, Confirmed, via Hyosung Heavy Industries newsroom, 16 Nov 2026; SK Telecom newsroom; Seoul Economic Daily; The Elec] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Spain: Box2Bit drops its last Aragon data centre project and sells the 150 MW grid connection to Blackstone
item.description: DCD reported on 16 November 2026 that Box2Bit, a Capital Energy subsidiary, has withdrawn from the Epilon data centre project in Épila, Aragon, and is selling the 150 MW of grid connection capacity it obtained for the project to Blackstone. Red Eléctrica had denied its subsidiary consumption access at the Calatorao 220 kV substation; Box2Bit's other two Aragon campuses (the €3.4 billion Ebro Campus in Cariñena and the €1 billion La Charluca site in Calatayud) were already ruled out for lack of transmission access. The 150 MW goes to Blackstone's Calatorao campus, which has final planning permission for 430 MW in two phases; El Español puts the associated investment above €13 billion. Épila's mayor says Box2Bit failed to make the first land payment and its land rights expired in May. Caveat: sale price is not disclosed and the report relies on DCD and El Español. Country conversion: in Spain, a granted grid connection is now a tradeable asset that moves from a stalled developer to a funded campus. [Signal 42, Single-source, via DCD, 16 Nov 2026; El Español] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Core Scientific files a $1.3 billion core-and-shell build in Hunt County, Texas, where AMD is set to lease 110 MW, as it exits bitcoin mining
item.description: A Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation filing by Telios Quinlan One LLC describes a $1.3 billion, 341,325 sq ft data centre core-and-shell building at Quinlan, Hunt County, about 53 miles northeast of Dallas, with construction from November 2026 to September 2028 (DCD, 16 November 2026). Core Scientific bought the 265-acre site in March for $232.5 million and says it can support up to 285 MW leasable (430 MW gross), energising from 2027 and fully powered by 2029; AMD is set to lease 110 MW there. On its 5 November Q3 call Core Scientific said it will complete its exit from bitcoin mining by year-end and enter 2027 as a high-density colocation provider; mining revenue fell to $17.4 million from $66.2 million a year earlier. Caveat: the filing covers one building, not the full 285 MW. Country conversion: in the US another miner's power is being converted to AI colocation with a chipmaker as anchor tenant. [Signal 40, Confirmed, via TDLR filing via DCD, 16 Nov 2026; Core Scientific Q3 2026 call and 10-Q] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: India: AirTrunk signs an MoU with Andhra Pradesh for 1.8 GW across two campuses near Visakhapatnam
item.description: AirTrunk said on 14 November 2026 that it signed a memorandum of understanding with Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu for two proposed data centre campuses in Anakapalli district: 400 MW at Rambilli and 1.4 GW at Tootipala, both outside Visakhapatnam (DCD, citing AirTrunk's LinkedIn post). Indian media put the proposed investment at about ₹1.03 lakh crore (about $11 billion); AirTrunk has not confirmed a figure. AirTrunk, owned by Blackstone and CPP Investments, entered India earlier this year by acquiring Lumina CloudInfra. The company says the campuses would use low-water, air-cooled designs and industrial water supply. Caveat: an MoU only; no land, power allocation, customer or timeline is disclosed. Country conversion: Andhra Pradesh adds a second hyperscale-scale commitment after Google's $15 billion Vizag AI hub, concentrating India's proposed AI capacity on the Vizag coast. [Signal 44, Confirmed, via AirTrunk (LinkedIn), 14 Nov 2026; DCD; NewsBytes] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Japan: Digital Realty plans $10 billion with Mitsubishi to take Japan capacity from 193 MW to about 700 MW over a decade
item.description: Digital Realty CEO Andy Power told Nikkei (published 14 November 2026 in Japanese, 15 November in Nikkei Asia) that the company will invest $10 billion in Japan over the next ten years through MC Digital Realty, its 50/50 joint venture with Mitsubishi Corp., lifting Japanese capacity from 193 MW to about 700 MW. Japan is its top Asian investment destination; it has invested about $4 billion there so far, and the new capacity will prioritise AI inference. The JV began building KIX15, a 24 MW Osaka facility, in October, due online in Q4 2028. Caveat: an interview, not a company release; the split between Digital Realty and Mitsubishi is not disclosed. Country conversion: Japan is drawing decade-long inference capacity commitments from global operators, with grid connections rather than capital named as the constraint. [Signal 40, Corroborated, via Nikkei / Nikkei Asia interview with CEO Andy Power, 14 to 15 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Canada: Telus pulls out of Westbank's two Vancouver AI data centres; Westbank says a new partner will continue
item.description: Telus confirmed to Daily Hive on 14 November 2026 that it will not proceed with co-developing two Vancouver AI data centres with Westbank: the conversion of the M3 office building at 111 East 5th Avenue and a new building at 150 West Georgia Street. Westbank said it is proceeding with a new, unnamed partner. The projects were part of Telus's May 2026 sovereign AI cluster plan, which started from 85 MW of BC Hydro power and targeted more than 150 MW by 2032. Telus gave no reason; the sites faced local protests, M3 still needs a rezoning (consultation scheduled 2 to 15 December), and October civic elections changed Vancouver's council. Caveat: the new partner is not named and the BC Hydro allocation's status is not disclosed. Country conversion: Canada's sovereign AI build loses its national telco sponsor at the urban sites, shifting execution to a private developer. [Signal 38, Corroborated, via Daily Hive (Telus and Westbank statements), 14 Nov 2026; DCD, 16 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire
